body.statement: Let \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\) satisfy \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\), and suppose \(x\to y\) is in \(G\) while \(y\to x\) is in \(H\). Then \(\mathcal N_x(C)=\mathcal N_y(C)\). Specifically, if \(S\in\mathcal N_x(C)\) is split across two blocks of \(\Pi_y\), choosing unit innovation variances, coefficient one on \(x\to y\), coefficient one on a block \(T\in\Pi_y\) meeting but not containing \(S\), and zero elsewhere gives a covariance in \(\mathcal M(C)\) whose regression of \(X_x\) on \(\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\) has coefficient \(-q\mathbf 1\{s\in T\}\) on \(s\in S\), with \(q=(2+|T\setminus(\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\setminus\{y\})|)^{-1}>0\), contradicting the block \(S\) in \(D\).
body.justification: This sparse covariance witness is the load-bearing necessity step because it handles arbitrary extra target parents and simultaneous arrow changes.
body.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Lemma 5.11 and the proof of Theorem 5.17, separates reversals only in the proper-colouring regime; it does not establish the endpoint-family condition when singleton blocks coexist with repeated blocks.
body.consumer: The separator certifies when a proposed singleton reversal changes the complete covariance model, preventing a learner from merging observationally distinguishable causal-community states.
